newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish troops consolidate hold on north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkish troops consolidate hold on north Iraq.

text.p: Turkey consolidated its hold in northern Iraq on Sunday, bringing a strategic valley under control in its cross-border offensive against Kurdish separatists, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
Turkish forces brought the Zap Valley in Iraq fully under control after five days of fierce fighting in the area, Anatolian quoted General Altay Tokat as saying.

Military authorities opened the region to selected Turkish journalists and film crews, giving them a tour of the Zap Valley over the weekend. Otherwise a ban on correspondents, imposed at the start of the 11-day-old operation, remained in force.
Television pictures showed two bodies, said to be those of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels, and large amounts of ammunition the army said it had captured from the guerrillas.
Tokat said 1,750 rebels had been killed or wounded in the operation so far. Western diplomats say the figures are inflated.

More than 10,000 Turkish troops, allied with the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), have poured into northern Iraq in pursuit of PKK rebels who use northern Iraq as a base to launch raids into southeast Turkey.
An armoured unit of around 1,000 men entered Iraq in the early hours of Saturday through the Turkish border town of Silopi, witnesses said.
The Turkish authorities have yet to give any figure for the total number of troops currently in Iraq.
Turkey has attracted international criticism for its drive in its attempt to quash PKK rebels who use the so-called Kurdish safe area, created after the 1991 Gulf War, to launch raids into Turkey.
Turkey mounted a six-week, 35,000-man operation into the Kurdish-held northern Iraqi regions two years ago but failed to achieve its stated aim of clearing the area of PKK.
